q: Under reverse charge, who pays the GST to the government?
exp: Reverse charge shifts the liability to the recipient.

q: What's the difference between section 9(3) and 9(4) of the CGST Act?
options: 9(3) is for goods and 9(4) is for services
9(3) covers notified supplies regardless of supplier; 9(4) covers notified supplies by unregistered suppliers to notified classes of registered persons
exp: 9(4) today applies to specific cases like promoters of real estate buying from unregistered persons.

q: RCM liability can be paid using ITC available in the electronic credit ledger.
exp: RCM tax must be paid in cash. You can then claim ITC of that tax (if eligible) in the same return.
ref: CGST Act, s.49(4) read with s.2(82)

q: A person who only supplies services that are entirely under reverse charge doesn't need to register.
exp: Section 23(1)(b) exempts persons making only supplies where the recipient pays the entire tax.

q: Legal services by an advocate to a business entity are taxed under:
options: Reverse charge, the business entity pays
exp: Advocates and law firms don't charge GST to business entities; the recipient pays under RCM. Services to individuals and small businesses below the threshold are exempt.

q: A company pays sitting fees to an independent director. GST?
options: Company pays GST under reverse charge
exp: Services by a director to the company are under RCM. Salary to a whole-time director as an employee is outside GST.

q: Which of these services is under reverse charge when supplied to a body corporate?
exp: Sponsorship to a body corporate or partnership firm is under RCM.

q: An unregistered person rents a shop (commercial property) to a registered business. From 10 October 2024, GST is:
options: Not payable as the landlord is unregistered
Payable by the registered tenant under reverse charge
exp: This was added on the 54th Council's recommendation. Composition tenants were later excluded.

q: Renting of a residential dwelling to a registered person (for any use) is:
options: Under reverse charge, payable by the registered tenant
exp: From 18 July 2022. There's an exemption when a proprietor rents in personal capacity for residence.

q: A GTA (goods transport agency) that hasn't opted to pay tax itself transports goods for a registered factory. Who pays GST?
options: No one, GTA services are exempt
exp: GTA services to specified recipients (factories, companies, registered persons, etc.) are under RCM unless the GTA opts for forward charge.

q: Security services (supply of security personnel) by an individual or firm (not a body corporate) to a registered person are:
exp: Added from 1 January 2019, with exclusions for certain recipients like composition taxpayers.

q: Services by an insurance agent to an insurance company are:
options: Reverse charge, the insurance company pays
exp: Similarly, recovery agents to banks or NBFCs and business facilitators to banks are under RCM.

q: An Indian company imports consultancy services from a UK firm. How is GST paid?
options: Indian company pays IGST under reverse charge
UK firm registers and charges IGST
exp: Import of services (other than OIDAR to non-business recipients) is under RCM for the importer.

q: In Mohit Minerals (2022), the Supreme Court held what about IGST on ocean freight under reverse charge for CIF imports?
options: It's unconstitutional, because it's part of a composite supply of goods already taxed at import
It's payable by the shipping line
It's payable at 5% on 10% of CIF value
exp: Taxing the freight separately would double-tax the composite supply. The entry was later omitted.
ref: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals, 2022

q: Which of these goods is under reverse charge?
options: Cashew nuts (not shelled) supplied by an agriculturist
exp: Raw cashew, bidi wrapper leaves, tobacco leaves, raw cotton from agriculturists and a few others are notified goods under RCM.

q: From October 2024, a registered person buying metal scrap from an unregistered supplier must:
exp: Metal scrap from unregistered persons was added to the RCM list, along with a TDS obligation for B2B scrap sales.

q: Used vehicles and seized goods sold by the government to a registered person are under reverse charge.
exp: The buyer pays GST under RCM.

q: Since November 2024, when a registered person receives RCM supplies from an unregistered supplier, it must issue a self-invoice within:
options: 30 days of receipt of the supply
At the end of the FY
exp: Rule 47A added a 30-day limit for self-invoices under section 31(3)(f).

q: What document does the recipient issue to the supplier when making payment under RCM?
exp: Section 31(3)(g).

q: Where is RCM liability reported in GSTR-3B?
options: Table 3.1(d), inward supplies liable to reverse charge
exp: The ITC on it goes in 4(A)(2) for import of services or 4(A)(3) for other RCM.

q: A composition taxpayer receiving a service under RCM must pay tax at the normal rate, not the composition rate.
exp: Composition rates apply only to outward supplies. RCM on inward supplies is at normal rates, and composition taxpayers can't take ITC.

q: Under section 9(5), which party pays GST on restaurant services ordered through a food delivery app (from 1 January 2022)?
exp: The ECO is treated as the supplier for these notified services.

q: Which of these is NOT notified under section 9(5)?
options: Passenger transport through a ride-hailing app
Accommodation services through an app (with some exceptions)
Housekeeping services like plumbing through an app
Sale of electronics through a marketplace
exp: Goods sales through marketplaces fall under TCS (s.52), not s.9(5).

q: An e-commerce operator paying tax under section 9(5) can use its ITC to pay that liability.
exp: Section 9(5) liability must be paid in cash. It's a liability the ECO discharges as a deemed supplier, and it can't be set off against the ECO's own credit.

q: A software company in Karnataka pays ₹5 lakh to a UK firm for market research and ₹50,000 as legal fees to an Indian advocate. What GST compliance does it need?
model: Both are under reverse charge. The UK research is an import of services: pay IGST at 18% (₹90,000) in cash under RCM, report in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d), and claim ITC in 4(A)(2). The advocate's fees: pay CGST+SGST at 18% (₹9,000) under RCM in cash, report in 3.1(d), and claim ITC in 4(A)(3). The advocate doesn't issue a GST invoice, so the company issues a self-invoice (within 30 days, since the advocate is typically unregistered) and a payment voucher.
points: Import of services: IGST under RCM
exp: ITC on RCM is usually available, so the net cost is cash flow, not tax.
ref: IGST Act, s.5(3); CGST Act, s.9(3)

q: During a GST audit, the officer finds a client paid ₹6 lakh to an advocate over the year without paying RCM. What does the client owe?
options: Nothing, the advocate should have charged GST
18% RCM on ₹6 lakh with interest; the ITC can then be claimed (subject to time limits)
exp: RCM paid late still generates ITC, but only if it's within the section 16(4) window. Interest is a real cost.
